title: Accommodation
subtitle: Where to stay in Nauru — hotels, guesthouses, and practical tips
intro: Nauru has limited but adequate accommodation options for visitors. The island offers a mix of government-run and private accommodations, ranging from standard hotel rooms to apartment-style units. Due to limited supply, advance booking is strongly recommended. Please note: accommodation availability and prices change frequently. Always verify current options directly with the property or through official sources.

sections.heading: Hotels
sections.content:
Menen Hotel — Nauru's largest and best-known hotel, located on the western coast near Anibare Bay. The Menen is a government-owned property offering comfortable rooms, a restaurant serving local and international cuisine, a bar, and conference facilities. It is the primary choice for business travellers and government visitors. Rooms are basic but clean, with air conditioning, private bathrooms, and some rooms offering ocean views.

The hotel has a mixed reputation — recent reviews note that while the location is excellent and staff are friendly, facilities can feel dated and maintenance is inconsistent.

OD-N-Aiwo Hotel — A smaller family-owned hotel in the Aiwo district, offering a more intimate experience. It has a limited number of rooms with essential amenities. The attached restaurant is popular with locals and visitors alike.

sections.heading: Alternative Accommodation
sections.content:
There are a few privately owned apartment-style units available for short-term rental. These offer more space and self-catering facilities (kitchenette, washing machine).

When making a booking inquiry, it's helpful to specify your preference for hotel or unit-style accommodation so the best available option can be arranged. Most bookings are handled directly via email or phone — online booking platforms rarely list Nauru properties.

sections.heading: Booking Tips
sections.content:
- Book well in advance (4–8 weeks recommended), especially if travelling during national holidays or events.
- Confirm your booking before purchasing flights — accommodation is limited.
- Most hotels do not accept online bookings through global platforms; contact them directly by email or phone.
- Payment is typically in Australian dollars (cash) or by bank transfer. Credit card acceptance is limited.
- Check whether your accommodation includes meals — some properties offer full board, others do not.

sections.heading: What to Expect
sections.content:
Accommodation in Nauru is functional rather than luxurious. Expect:
- Basic but clean rooms with essential furnishings
- Air conditioning (not always available in budget options)
- Limited Wi-Fi — internet connectivity can be slow and unreliable island-wide
- Cold-water showers in some budget accommodations
- Mosquito nets or screens (recommended during the wet season)
- Generators or backup power during occasional outages

The lack of high-end or resort-style accommodation reflects Nauru's status as an emerging destination — this is changing slowly as tourism interest grows.
